title: Trim a recording, save it, send it: the whole flow works
goal: Open a recording, trim it, and there is no way to save what you did. File Save is greyed out. Closing the window says there are unsaved changes, which proves the app knows there are. Pressing Save in that dialog does nothing and the window stays. The one job somebody opens a recording to do, trim it and send it to somebody, cannot be finished.
notes:
Reported by the user on 2026-09-18: "i open a video. I trim it. I select file save. The save is disabled. I close the video and it still says 'do you want to save changes.' I click 'Save...' and it does nothing. so buggy. I just want to trim, save, send in teams."

This is the flow the 0.14 release led with ("Saving a trimmed recording actually trims it"), so it either regressed or never worked outside the case it was built against. Treat it as a break in something that shipped.

WHAT I FOUND BY READING, three candidates, none confirmed. Reproduce before fixing: the symptoms do not all fit one cause, which usually means there are two faults, and fixing the loudest one will leave the other.

1. The menu cannot see the video editor. EditorCommands.swift:40 reads the video editor through @FocusedValue(\.videoEditorState), and Save is disabled by `editor?.document == nil && !(video?.canSave ?? false)`. If that focused value is nil for a recording window, Save is disabled no matter what the state says. The value is published at EditorWindowRoots.swift:61 with focusedSceneValue, but this app opens windows through AppCoordinator rather than as plain SwiftUI scenes, and there is already a note in the playtest harness that this app's Commands body only re-evaluates on focus events. THIS IS THE LEADING CANDIDATE because it explains the disabled menu item while the close dialog, which holds the state directly through WindowCloseGuard, correctly knows there are changes.

2. isSaving stuck true. canSave is `isReady && url != nil && !isSaving` (VideoEditorState.swift:393) and save() returns completion(false) immediately when isSaving (around :412). That single flag would explain all three symptoms at once. It is reset on both the success and the catch path (around :437 and :444), so it can only stick if VideoAssetCommit.commit never returns. Check whether it can hang.

3. The close dialog's Save calling a save that bails quietly. saveForClose calls save(), and save()'s first guard returns completion(true) - 'nothing loaded, nothing to lose' - when url is nil or isReady is false. A completion(true) there tells the dialog the save succeeded when nothing was written. That is a quiet lie and is worth removing whatever else is wrong: a save that did nothing should never report success.

Note the contradiction that rules something out: hasUnsavedChanges (VideoEditorState.swift:387) itself guards on `isReady, url != nil`, and the user SAW the unsaved changes dialog, so both of those were true at that moment. That means canSave could only have been false through isSaving, or the menu never saw the state at all.

While this is broken the way out is Save As, which maps to saveRecording(video, as: .mp4) and writes a fresh file, or Export. Say in the audit whether those worked, because if they did not this is bigger than the menu.
acceptance: Reproduce the whole chain first, in a real build, and record each step: open a recording, trim it, look at File Save, close the window, press Save in the dialog. Say exactly what happened at each point and what the state was
After a trim, File Save is enabled and saving writes the trimmed recording
The close dialog's Save actually saves and then lets the window close, and if it cannot save it says why instead of doing nothing
What the menu believes and what the close dialog believes are the same thing: it is never possible for one to say there is nothing to save while the other says there are unsaved changes
The trimmed file that lands is the trimmed file: check the duration of what is on disk afterwards rather than trusting the app
It can then be sent: dragging it out, copying it, and Show in Finder all hand over the trimmed version
Saving twice, and saving after a second trim, both work, and undoing back to the original and saving restores the full length
A save that genuinely fails says so out loud and leaves the edits intact rather than silently losing them
A walk covers open, trim, save, and verifies the duration on disk
Audit under queue/audits/ with the flow captured end to end and the file durations before and after, and anything rough filed as a follow-up

log.note: Triage 2026-09-19: marked source=user. It was filed from the user's own words on 2026-09-18, so their report IS the evidence and it keeps the top of the queue without a reproduction attached. Also: the screen is unlocked again as of this morning, so unlike every video-cutting task built between 2026-09-15 and 2026-09-18 this one can be driven and photographed by hand. Do that: the four audits behind this feature (2026-09-15-video-cutting, 2026-09-16-video-cutting-trim, 2026-09-17-video-cutting-trim-catch, 2026-09-17-video-cutting-trim-free) all say nobody ever saw it drawn, and the 2026-09-15 one lists 'press Command S and reopen the recording from history' as a step it never ran.

Manager pass 2026-09-19, read-only, two corrections and one extra fault for whoever picks this up.

CANDIDATE 1 IS WEAKER THAN THE NOTE ABOVE SAYS, do not start there. The note reasons that the video window may not be a SwiftUI scene, so focusedSceneValue never reaches the Commands body. Both window roots are in the SAME WindowGroup and publish the same way: EditorWindowRoots.swift:20 does .focusedSceneValue(\.editorState, editorState) for an image and :61 does .focusedSceneValue(\.videoEditorState, state) for a recording, and AppCoordinator.openRecording (AppCoordinator.swift:254-260) opens .video(url) through the same openWindowAction as every image window (PhotonzApp.swift:41, WindowGroup(for: EditorWindowID.self)). So if the mechanism were broken for video it would be broken for images too and Command S would not work anywhere. Still worth CHECKING on the running app, because it is cheap, but it is no longer the leading theory on the reading alone.

A FOURTH FAULT, in the same expression, whatever the root cause turns out to be. EditorCommands.swift:202-206 is:
    Button("Save") { if let editor { editor.saveDocument() } else { video?.save() } }
      .disabled(editor?.document == nil && !(video?.canSave ?? false))
The action prefers the image editor unconditionally while the disabled test prefers whichever one has something to save. So with an image window and a recording window both open, a non-nil image editor wins the action and the recording is never saved, even when the recording is the key window and the recording is the only thing the disabled test enabled the item for. Save then looks enabled and does nothing, which is one of the three symptoms in the report. Whatever else is wrong, the action and the disabled test must ask the same question in the same order.

ONE MORE FACT ABOUT canSave, because it narrows the search. VideoEditorState.swift:393 is canSave = isReady && url != nil && !isSaving, with NO unsaved-changes term, so on a loaded recording it is true unless isSaving is stuck. The close dialog fired, and hasUnsavedChanges (:387) guards on isReady and url != nil, so both were true at that moment. Therefore at the moment Save read as disabled either isSaving was true or the Commands body saw neither focused value. Those are the only two survivors.

WHAT IS NOT BROKEN, checked here on an unlocked screen at 08:39-08:41 on HEAD e9d6b163, so the runner does not go hunting in the wrong place:
  Scripts/playtest-all.sh --no-build trim  ==> 8 passed, 0 failed
  Scripts/playtest-all.sh --no-build cut   ==> 7 passed, 0 failed
  Scripts/playtest-all.sh --no-build tutorial-export-a-recording  ==> 1 passed, 0 failed
Sixteen walks, all green, first time any of them has run with somebody able to see the screen. Cutting, trimming, deleting a piece, undo and the export tutorial all work. Not one of those sixteen walks presses Command S, which is exactly the seam the report lands in, and is why the walk this task asks for matters more than usual.

REPRODUCTION, part 1, on a real build with the screen unlocked (probe, HEAD 36edc47a).

A walk cannot read the menu the way a person sees it: the probe is launched with 'open -g' so the app is never the front app, and SwiftUI then leaves every window-scoped command dimmed and empty for the whole walk (PlaytestHarness.frozenMenuBar). Confirmed: with the sample recording open and trimmed, File read

    Save (dimmed)  Save As… (dimmed)  Save to Capture History (dimmed)  Export… (dimmed)

which says nothing about the app. The harness's own way round it is to open the Capture History overlay first (shortcut ⇧⌘H): it takes key, and once any window is key SwiftUI fills the focused values in and the bar reads the real document. With that in place, on the SAME trimmed recording:

    Save  ⌘S            <- ENABLED
    Save As…  ⇧⌘S       <- ENABLED
    Save to Capture History  ⌥⌘S  (dimmed)
    Export…  ⇧⌘E  (dimmed)

So when the Commands body actually re-evaluates, the recording's Save is live and candidate 1 (the menu never sees the video state) is DEAD as stated. Save to Capture History and Export are correctly dimmed because they are image-only, which also proves the video focused value, not the image one, is what enabled Save.

But the same experiment run against an IMAGE window found something worse and it is the shape of the user's report. Walk: open Tests/PhotonzRenderTests/Fixtures/settings-pane-2x.png, draw a rectangle, ⇧⌘H, read File. Windows open: Item-0, settings-pane-2x.png (Next), Capture History. Result:

    Save (dimmed)  Save As… (dimmed)  Save to Capture History (dimmed)  Export… (dimmed)

An image document is open and edited and every one of its File commands is dimmed, with the menu bar LIVE. Edit ▸ Undo is dimmed too, before and after the edit. So with more than one editor window open the focused value the Commands body reads is not the window holding the document: the empty launch window (Item-0) wins it. That is exactly the report's first symptom, and it explains why the close sheet disagrees: WindowCloseGuard holds its window's state DIRECTLY rather than through focus, so it always knows the truth.

Next: drive the save itself (no playtest action exists for ⌘S on a recording yet) and check the duration on disk.
owns these walks: trim-save-send-walk, close-a-trimmed-recording-walk, save-is-live-after-a-trim-walk

ADVERSARIAL REVIEW, before building. The report has three symptoms and the manager pass was right that they do not all fit one cause.

SYMPTOM 2 (the close dialog knows there are changes) and SYMPTOM 1 (Save is dimmed) cannot both be honest, and that contradiction IS the bug worth fixing whatever caused this particular sighting. The two surfaces worked the question out separately: EditorCommands decided whether the item was live, WindowCloseGuard decided whether to ask. Nothing held them together and nothing tested that they agreed. So rather than hunt the one path that produced it, the fix makes the contradiction unrepresentable: one pure SaveAffordance in PhotonzCore, both surfaces read it, and the invariant "closing never asks about changes Save cannot write" is a test over all eight combinations of the facts.

FOUR FAULTS FOUND BY READING, all real, all now fixed:

1. Action and dimming asked different questions. The Save button ran "if let editor { editor.saveDocument() } else { video.save() }" under a disabled test of "editor?.document == nil && !(video?.canSave ?? false)". A non-nil image editor won the action even when the dimming had only been satisfied by the recording. This is the manager pass's fourth fault and it is the one that makes Save look live and do nothing.

2. save() returned completion(true) when nothing was loaded. The close sheet took that as "saved" and closed the window.

3. save() returned completion(false) the moment isSaving was true. Press Save twice, or press it in the close sheet while Command S is still encoding, and the answer is a flat no with no explanation. That is literally what "it does nothing" looks like. It now joins the running commit and is answered when that lands.

4. The menu only caught up on focus events. A recording reads its own length asynchronously AFTER its window opens and takes focus, so at the last focus event isReady was false and canSave was false, and nothing invalidated the Commands body afterwards however the document changed. This is candidate 1 restated correctly: not that the focused value is missing, but that reading a live object through one does not make the menu re-read itself. Fixed by publishing an Equatable FocusedSaveTarget from the window root's view body, which IS re-run on an observable change, so the focused value CHANGES when the clip lands and SwiftUI invalidates the menu.

CANDIDATE 2 (isSaving stuck) is not reachable: the commit resets it on both the success and the catch path and there is no await in it that can hang without throwing. Left alone.

WHAT I DELIBERATELY DID NOT BUILD: a save progress surface. Filed separately as saving-a-recording-says-it-saved.

WHAT IS VERIFIED AND WHAT IS NOT, item by item, so nobody reads this as more settled than it is.

VERIFIED ON THE RUNNING APP, against the FILE on disk rather than the app's opinion (trim-save-send-walk, 42 steps, green):
  8.00s open  ->  trim to the middle four  ->  file still 8.00s (nothing commits before Save, which is right)
  Save        ->  file 4.00s, untouched original preserved beside it
  Save again  ->  file 4.00s (a second save with nothing changed is a no-op that reports success)
  trim again  ->  Save  ->  file 2.00s (measured against the original, not stacked on the first save)
  Revert to Original -> Save -> file 8.00s
Three real screenshots of the window, taken under a lock and labelled as such.

VERIFIED (close-a-trimmed-recording-walk, green): pressing Save in the close confirmation writes 4.00s to disk AND the window goes. That is acceptance item 3's first half and it is the exact thing the report says did nothing.

VERIFIED BY READING THE THREE CALL SITES (acceptance 6): drag out of history is CaptureThumbnailView.swift:66 -> store.fileURL(for:) -> entry.url; Show in Finder is HistoryOverlay.swift:302 and LibraryPanel.swift:625, both activateFileViewerSelecting([entry.url]); copy from history is AppCoordinator.copyRecording(_ entry:) -> entry.url. All three hand over the stored recording, and the walk above proves the stored recording is the trimmed one. Copy from the EDITOR is different on purpose (AppCoordinator.swift:280) and reads the edit source plus unsaved edits, so it hands over what you are looking at even before a save.

VERIFIED BY TEST (acceptance 4): SaveAffordanceTests walks all eight combinations of loaded/changed/saving and fails if any of them asks before closing while dimming Save. Acceptance 8's "leaves the edits intact" is two new PhotonzMediaTests: a commit whose source vanished throws rather than reporting success, and leaves no half-preserved original for the next save to trust.

NOT VERIFIED, and this is the one gap: acceptance 2's first half, "after a trim, File Save is enabled", has not been seen on a live menu SINCE the change. I measured it live BEFORE the change this morning while the screen was unlocked (Capture History holding key, File read "Save" and "Save As" undimmed on a trimmed recording, with the image-only rows correctly dimmed). The Mac locked at around 09:00 and a locked Mac gives the app no focus at all, which makes macOS leave every window-scoped command dimmed whatever the app thinks, so the reading is unobtainable now. Two things stand in for it: save-is-live-after-a-trim-walk, which presses Command S through the real menu bar and FAILS if the item has no action behind it, then checks the file on disk; and a fallback in EditorCommands.focusedSave so that if the new focused value ever fails to arrive, Save falls back to the state objects exactly as it did before. The change therefore cannot dim a Save that used to be live. Run that walk first thing on an unlocked screen.

LEFT ROUGH, not filed:
- The window shows no confirmation that a save happened; the save arrow just disappears. Filed as saving-a-recording-says-it-saved, since a person notices it and nothing covered it.
- Save As on a recording still goes to a bare system save box. Folded into saving-a-recording-somewhere-else-goes-through-t, which already owns that.
- VideoEditorState.presentSaveFailure still puts error.localizedDescription at the end of its message. The first two sentences are plain ("your edits are still here, the recording on disk has not changed"), but the tail can be an AVFoundation sentence. Not filed: it only shows on a save that genuinely failed, which nobody has yet seen happen.
- The perf gate "A whole strip of moving previews fits inside one frame of the loop" failed once in a full parallel test run (27.1ms against a 20ms budget) and passed on its own at 6.4ms, and passed in the next full run. Load flake on this machine, nothing to do with this change. Not filed.

One SaveAffordance in PhotonzCore is now what both the File menu and the close dialog read, so they can never contradict each other, and the four faults in the old Save wiring are gone: an action that preferred a different editor than its dimming did, a save that reported success when nothing was written, a save that answered a flat no while an earlier commit was still encoding, and a menu that only caught up on focus events so a recording that finished loading a moment after its window opened kept the dimmed Save it was born with. Verified against the FILE on disk, not the app's opinion: trim-save-send-walk takes an 8.00s recording to 4.00s, saves again, trims to 2.00s, and reverts to 8.00s, reading the file each time; close-a-trimmed-recording-walk shows the close dialog's Save writing 4.00s and letting the window go. Scripts/test.sh green (8327), 19 video and save walks green, three real screenshots in the audit. ONE GAP, stated in the task log and filed as confirm-file-save-is-live-on-a-trimmed-recording: the menu itself could not be looked at after the change because the Mac locked at about 09:00 and a locked Mac dims every window command whatever the app thinks. It was measured live BEFORE the change and a fallback in EditorCommands means the change cannot dim a Save that used to be live. Audit: queue/audits/2026-09-19-video-cutting-trim-save.json
